claims: A Grade 2 hamstring strain is a partial tear of the muscle.
A Grade 2 hamstring strain causes significant pain, swelling, and temporary loss of function.
Recovery from a Grade 2 hamstring strain typically takes 4–6 weeks.
Expert estimates suggest an average of 35 days for athletes recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
Aaron Gordon Injury: Hamstring Strain says 4-6 weeks is the typical healing time for a partial tear.
A report from Yahoo Sports indicates experts say elite athletes miss an average of 35 days due to hamstring strain.
Sports Medicine Australia outlines the RICER protocol (Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation, Referral) for immediate (0-72 hours) treatment to manage inflammation.
The NHS says to avoid HARM (Heat, Alcohol, Running, Massage) for the first 3 days.
Temple Health says gentle stretches and progressive strength exercises (like bridges) are introduced once pain allows.
Nemours KidsHealth notes high risk of reinjury if returning too quickly.
OrthoInfo suggests focus on eccentric strengthening for long-term recovery
